chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah have mercy on him - from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from his father. And I have transmitted it from Ja'far ibn Ali ibn Al-Hasan Al-Kufi, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the author's father
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ الْكُوفِيِّ: Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, a specific narrator
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Ja'far ibn Ali, another narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: How did the author transmit narrations from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs this passage to demonstrate the reliability of Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi by presenting two independent transmission chains (tawatur), one through his father and another through his grandfather, thereby reinforcing the authenticity of the narrations in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. This methodological rigor reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying the integrity of the narrator's lineage and scholarly connection to the Imams. By cross-referencing these paths, al-Saduq ensures that the legal rulings derived from these hadiths are grounded in a robust and verifiable chain of authority.
